# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Plain-language definitions of the terms used in this book, in alphabetical order. Where a term is explained in a chapter, the chapter is noted.

**Accuracy.** The share of all predictions that were correct. Misleading when one answer is much more common than the other, because "always guess the common one" scores well (@sec-supervised).

**Alpha (in LDA).** A setting that controls how mixed each document's topics are. Small values push each document toward one or two topics (@sec-lda).

**Anti-join.** A way of combining two tables that keeps only the rows of the first table that have *no* match in the second. We use it to remove stop words (@sec-tokens).

**AUC (area under the curve).** A threshold-free score for how well a model ranks "yes" cases above "no" cases. 0.5 is guessing and 1.0 is perfect (@sec-supervised).

**Beta (in topic models).** For each topic, the probability of each word. The words with the highest beta define what the topic is about (@sec-lda).

**Bigram.** A pair of neighboring words, such as "financial aid." A trigram has three words, and in general an *n-gram* has *n* (@sec-tokens).

**Coefficient.** A number that says how strongly something pushes a prediction. In a regression, it is the estimated difference in the outcome. In the lasso, most coefficients are zero, and the nonzero ones identify the important words (@sec-stm, @sec-supervised).

**Confidence interval.** A range of values that plausibly contains the true quantity. We draw 95% intervals as error bars: the average plus or minus 1.96 standard errors (@sec-sentiment).

**Confusion matrix.** A 2×2 table counting a classifier's hits, misses, false alarms, and correct rejections (@sec-supervised).

**Cosine similarity.** A score from -1 to 1 for how closely two vectors point in the same direction. For embeddings, high means similar meaning. When vectors are scaled to length 1, it equals their dot product (@sec-embeddings).

**Covariate.** A characteristic of a document or person that you want to relate to the outcome, such as a student's level (@sec-stm).

**Cross-validation.** Estimating how well a model will do on new data by repeatedly training on part of the training data and testing on the rest. `cv.glmnet()` uses it to pick the penalty strength (@sec-supervised).

**Data frame / tibble.** A table where each row is an observation and each column is a variable. A tibble is the tidyverse's version (@sec-r-primer).

**Data leakage.** Information from the test data accidentally influencing the model, which makes test results look better than they would be on genuinely new data (@sec-supervised).

**Dimension.** One position in a vector. MiniLM's embeddings have 384 dimensions (@sec-embeddings).

**Document.** Whatever unit of text you decide to treat as one piece: an answer, a student, a question. Your choice shapes every result (@sec-data).

**Document-term matrix.** A grid with one row per document and one column per word, with word counts in the cells (@sec-lda).

**Embedding.** A list of numbers that represents a text so that texts with similar meanings get similar numbers. It is like an address on a map of meaning (@sec-embeddings).

**F1.** A single score that balances precision and recall. It is low whenever either one is low (@sec-supervised).

**Factor.** A column with a fixed set of allowed categories in a stated order (@sec-data, @sec-stm).

**Few-shot learning.** Learning a task from only a small number of labeled examples. Pretrained models often make this possible (@sec-embeddings).

**FREX.** A way of ranking a topic's words by how both *frequent* and *exclusive* to the topic they are. Useful for naming topics (@sec-stm).

**Function.** A named recipe: you give it inputs (arguments) and it returns a result (@sec-r-primer).

**Gamma (in topic models).** For each document, how much of it belongs to each topic. A document's gammas sum to 1 (@sec-lda).

**IDF (inverse document frequency).** A rarity score for a word: high when the word appears in few documents, zero when it appears in all of them (@sec-tfidf).

**K.** The number of topics a topic model is asked to find. You choose it (@sec-lda).

**Label noise.** Errors or disagreement in the human-assigned labels that a supervised model learns from. It limits how well any model can do (@sec-supervised).

**Lambda.** The strength of the penalty in a regularized regression. Chosen by cross-validation (@sec-supervised).

**Lasso.** A regularized regression that shrinks most coefficients all the way to zero, leaving a short list of important words (@sec-supervised).

**LDA (Latent Dirichlet Allocation).** The most common topic model. It describes each document as a mix of topics and each topic as a list of words (@sec-lda).

**Learning curve.** A chart of how a model's performance changes as it is given more training examples. Used to see how many labeled examples a method needs (@sec-embeddings).

**Lexicon.** A word list with labels attached, such as which words are positive or negative, or which words are stop words (@sec-tokens, @sec-sentiment).

**Lift.** How many times more common something is in one group than overall. 1 means no difference; 2 means twice as common (@sec-lda).

**Log-likelihood.** A score for how well a model fits the data. Higher is better, but it always improves as you add topics, so it cannot choose K by itself (@sec-lda).

**Median.** The middle value: half the values are smaller and half larger. Less affected by extreme values than the mean (@sec-data).

**Multi-label.** A prediction problem where each item can have several labels at once, such as an answer coded with more than one topic (@sec-supervised).

**Negation.** Words like "not" and "never" that flip a meaning. Simple lexicon methods cannot see them (@sec-sentiment).

**Overfitting.** A model that learns the quirks of its training data so well that it does poorly on new data (@sec-supervised).

**Perplexity.** A measure of how well a topic model predicts documents it has not seen. Lower is better (@sec-lda).

**Pipe (`|>`).** R's "and then" symbol. It passes what is on its left into the function on its right (@sec-r-primer).

**Precision.** Of the cases a model flags as "yes," the share that really are. "When it says yes, can I trust it?" (@sec-supervised).

**Pretrained model.** A model that has already learned from a huge amount of text before you use it, so that you can borrow what it learned instead of starting from nothing (@sec-embeddings).

**Prevalence (in STM).** How much of the text belongs to a topic. STM lets prevalence depend on covariates (@sec-stm).

**Recall.** Of the cases that really are "yes," the share the model found. "How many did it catch?" (@sec-supervised).

**Regression.** A method for estimating how an outcome changes with something else. The result is a coefficient (@sec-stm).

**Regular expression (regex).** A compact pattern language for searching text, such as `^\\d+$` for "only digits" (@sec-r-primer).

**Regularization.** Adding a penalty on the size of a model's coefficients so it does not overfit (@sec-supervised).

**Seed.** The starting point of R's random number generator. Setting it makes random steps reproducible (@sec-r-primer).

**Sentiment.** How positive or negative language is (@sec-sentiment).

**Sparse matrix.** A grid that is mostly zeros, stored compactly by recording only the non-zero cells (@sec-lda, @sec-supervised).

**Standard error.** A measure of how uncertain an estimate (such as an average) is. Shrinks as the group gets larger (@sec-sentiment).

**Stemming / lemmatizing.** Reducing words to a root or dictionary form, so "advisor," "advisors," and "advising" count as one (@sec-tokens).

**STM (structural topic model).** A topic model that lets topic prevalence depend on document characteristics (@sec-stm).

**Stop words.** Very common function words ("the," "and," "of") removed before counting (@sec-tokens).

**Supervised learning.** Training a model on examples with known answers, then testing it on examples it has not seen (@sec-supervised).

**TF (term frequency).** How common a word is within a document (@sec-tfidf).

**TF-IDF.** TF multiplied by IDF. High for words that are frequent in one document and rare in the others (@sec-tfidf).

**Threshold.** The cutoff probability above which a model's prediction becomes "yes." Changing it trades precision against recall (@sec-supervised).

**Token.** The unit of text you count, usually a word (@sec-tokens).

**Topic.** In a topic model, a list of words that tend to appear together. A topic is not a label; you name it yourself by reading its words (@sec-lda).

**Transformer.** The kind of neural network behind modern language models. MiniLM is a small one (@sec-embeddings).

**Unsupervised learning.** Finding patterns in data without an answer key (@sec-lda).

**Vector.** A list of numbers. An answer's embedding is a vector (@sec-embeddings).

**Vocabulary.** The set of distinct words a model works with, often after dropping very rare ones (@sec-lda, @sec-supervised).

**Zero-shot learning.** Classifying with no labeled examples, by describing the categories and asking a model how well each text fits them (@sec-wrapup).
